incident: The host times out connecting to huggingface.co on port 443, so config.json and weights cannot be downloaded. Other local applications are healthy.
notes: B matches the reference cause and both actions; A mislabels the cause and only one action is useful.

incident: Serving retries a model repository HEAD request and then reports network unreachable. A verified snapshot can be transferred from another machine.
notes: A is complete and correct; B gives the wrong cause and unrelated remediation.

incident: Corporate egress blocks the model registry, and no files exist in the local cache. DNS for unrelated sites succeeds.
notes: Both identify the cause; A includes both expected actions while B replaces the mirror action with a secondary check.

incident: The model Hub connection is reset on every download attempt, while a domestic mirror is reachable and the intended revision is known.
notes: B fully matches the expected diagnosis and recovery; A omits both primary recovery actions.

incident: An offline inference node has no cached model artifact and cannot reach the remote repository. The service configuration itself is valid.
notes: Both are useful; B covers both expected actions while A substitutes snapshot verification for mirror configuration.

incident: QLoRA training fails on the first backward pass with CUDA out of memory. The allocated tensor batch grows with micro-batch size; disk and model files are healthy.
notes: Both diagnose CUDA OOM; B includes gradient checkpointing while A suggests an inference-oriented concurrency change.

incident: A fine-tuning job succeeds with micro-batch 1 but fails with micro-batch 8 while allocating optimizer activations. The error explicitly says CUDA out of memory.
notes: A covers both expected training mitigations; B omits gradient checkpointing.

incident: During adapter training, reserved GPU memory reaches the device limit and backward cannot allocate another 900 MiB. No inference server is running.
notes: B is complete; A correctly reduces batch size but uses a less relevant concurrency action for training.

incident: The trainer loads correctly, then OOMs only after increasing per-device train batch size. Sequence length and package versions are unchanged.
notes: A matches both expected mitigations; B provides a reasonable but different memory reduction.

incident: PyTorch reports CUDA out of memory in the backward graph for a QLoRA run. Smaller batches previously completed on the same GPU and driver.
notes: A is complete; B diagnoses correctly but omits gradient checkpointing.

incident: vllm bench crashes because datasets expects pyarrow.PyExtensionType, which was removed by the installed PyArrow release.
notes: A exactly addresses the dependency conflict; B identifies the class but recommends model-file checks.

incident: Installing an unrelated package upgraded transformers beyond the range required by the serving stack; imports now fail before CUDA initialization.
notes: A is complete; B misdiagnoses the import failure as a model artifact problem.

incident: pip reports incompatible requirements for tokenizers and transformers, and the benchmark CLI fails during module import.
notes: B gives the expected dependency recovery; A identifies the cause but offers incomplete and partly irrelevant actions.

incident: The environment contains packages from two experiments with mutually incompatible pydantic versions. A clean lockfile installation works elsewhere.
notes: Both identify and pin the conflict; B also rebuilds the environment as required.

incident: A partial package upgrade leaves vLLM and its benchmark extras on incompatible versions, producing an AttributeError at startup.
notes: A is complete; B omits environment recreation and substitutes a model-file check.

incident: Downloading model shards stops with No space left on device. GPU memory is unused and the network remains connected.
notes: B gives both storage remedies; A diagnoses correctly but adds an unrelated concurrency reduction.

incident: The Hugging Face cache partition is 100% full and cannot write a temporary safetensors shard.
notes: A is complete; B omits moving the cache to the available storage.

incident: Checkpoint saving fails with errno 28 after training, although RAM and VRAM have free capacity.
notes: A correctly identifies disk exhaustion and frees space; B incorrectly treats errno 28 as GPU OOM.

incident: The root filesystem has only a few megabytes free, and model extraction fails while a larger mounted volume is available.
notes: A fully uses the larger volume; B diagnoses correctly but omits relocating the cache.

incident: A repeated experiment fills the cache with old snapshots, preventing the current model manifest from being written.
notes: Both misdiagnose filesystem exhaustion as KV-cache exhaustion and provide unusable remediation.

incident: torch.cuda.is_available is false and PyTorch says the installed NVIDIA driver is too old for the CUDA runtime bundled in the wheel.
notes: B covers both compatibility actions; A adds gradient checkpointing, which does not address the mismatch.

incident: Importing a CUDA extension fails with an undefined CUDA symbol after upgrading torch without changing the host driver.
notes: A correctly aligns the driver and Torch build; B misdiagnoses the symbol failure as OOM.

incident: nvidia-smi works, but the application reports that its CUDA runtime version is unsupported by the current driver branch.
notes: Both identify the mismatch; A includes the compatible Torch build while B substitutes a capability check.

incident: A newly installed cu130 torch wheel cannot initialize CUDA on a machine whose driver supports only an older runtime. Model files are local and valid.
notes: A is complete; B omits installing a build compatible with the older driver.

incident: The custom operator was compiled against a different CUDA major version than the active PyTorch build and fails to load its shared library.
notes: B addresses both binary compatibility layers; A substitutes a capability check for a matching Torch build.

incident: The vLLM engine rejects new 8K requests because no KV cache blocks are available at concurrency 16. Model weights remain loaded and short requests still finish.
notes: Both outputs exactly identify KV-cache exhaustion and provide both expected mitigations.

incident: Long-context traffic fills every GPU KV block; requests wait indefinitely while GPU model memory is otherwise stable. Lower concurrency avoids the issue.
notes: Both outputs are equally complete, correct, and safe.

incident: Startup reports enough room for only four 8192-token sequences, but the load test admits eight near-maximum prompts and stalls on cache allocation.
notes: Both correctly connect admitted long contexts to KV capacity and give both mitigations.

incident: Decode scheduling repeatedly preempts long requests because the KV cache has no free blocks. There is no CUDA allocator OOM during model loading.
notes: Both outputs fully match the reference diagnosis and actions.

incident: A serving workload is healthy at 2K context but reaches KV cache capacity at 8K context with the same number of users.
notes: Both outputs are identical in substance and fully correct.

incident: vLLM is given /models/qwen but config.json is actually under /models/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, so it reports that the local path is not a valid model.
notes: A uses the precise invalid-path cause; B suggests the right checks but uses the wrong cause label.

incident: The configured local directory exists but contains only a README and no config.json or safetensors files.
notes: B precisely diagnoses the invalid local path; A has useful actions but labels it as artifact unavailability.

incident: A relative model path resolves from the wrong working directory and vLLM cannot find tokenizer.json in that location.
notes: A includes snapshot verification; B is useful but replaces it with a redundant path-verification action.

incident: The service points at a parent cache directory instead of the pinned snapshot directory containing config.json and model shards.
notes: B directly corrects the pinned snapshot path; A mislabels the cause and does not correct the path.

incident: Startup says the supplied path is missing configuration files; network access is intentionally disabled because the model should be local.
notes: A fully addresses the bad local path; B mislabels the issue and omits path correction.

incident: An unbounded burst sends hundreds of requests to a healthy service; queue time and P95 TTFT explode while each completed request is correct.
notes: A includes admission control and a concurrency cap; B omits explicit admission control.

incident: Latency SLO failures occur only when arrival rate exceeds sustainable throughput. GPU memory and model artifacts remain stable.
notes: B fully addresses overload at the gateway; A provides a useful concurrency reduction but not admission control.

incident: The API accepts every request during a traffic spike, causing a long queue and timeouts without engine crashes.
notes: B directly prevents unbounded admission; A treats concurrency but omits the admission mechanism.

incident: A load test with unlimited concurrency drives goodput toward zero because most requests miss TTFT SLO despite nonzero raw throughput.
notes: A matches both expected controls; B is useful but incomplete.

incident: The service is fast at controlled concurrency but degrades sharply when the gateway removes its request limit and admits a large burst.
notes: A restores gateway admission control and caps concurrency; B omits the first control.

incident: The selected FP8 kernel reports that the GPU architecture does not support the requested precision mode, while BF16 starts successfully.
notes: Both outputs exactly match the unsupported-precision diagnosis and safe fallback actions.

incident: Starting with an experimental cache dtype fails an architecture capability check before any requests arrive; using bfloat16 avoids the failure.
notes: A is complete; B misdiagnoses the capability failure as OOM despite one relevant check.

incident: A quantized attention backend requires a newer compute capability than the installed GPU and rejects initialization.
notes: Both use the wrong driver-mismatch cause; A is slightly more useful because it at least checks GPU capability.

incident: The engine can load model weights in BF16 but raises not implemented when KV cache dtype is changed to an unsupported low-precision format.
notes: Both correctly select a supported dtype and verify device capability.

incident: A low-precision execution path is unavailable for this device generation, and the same configuration works after selecting a supported dtype.
notes: Both outputs are equally complete and safe.

incident: The benchmark tokenizes prompts with a newer tokenizer revision than the server model snapshot, producing different token IDs for the same text.
notes: B pins the matching revision; A diagnoses correctly but substitutes a snapshot-file check.

incident: Requests fail alignment checks because the client uses a tokenizer from another Qwen model while the server uses Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.
notes: Both restore tokenizer consistency; B also pins the model revision as required.

incident: Prompt lengths measured by the benchmark disagree with server usage after only tokenizer files were updated in the local snapshot.
notes: B fully restores the controlled tokenizer revision; A offers only partial file verification and an unrelated environment rebuild.

incident: Special chat tokens are encoded as ordinary text because the client tokenizer revision does not match the pinned model revision.
notes: Both outputs exactly match the reference and are equally actionable.

incident: The server is offline-capable, but the benchmark silently downloads a different tokenizer and reports input lengths unlike the controlled run.
notes: A pins the controlled revision; B diagnoses correctly but omits revision pinning.
